responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the Renesas M32R family, covering the machine-specific code-generation, ABI, and system-integration logic needed to turn GCC’s generic RTL into correct M32R assembly. Its core is the combination of the main target header and hand-written backend implementation in m32r.h and m32r.c/m32r.cc, which define register layout, calling conventions, frame and prologue/epilogue handling, address legitimacy, symbol/section selection, PIC and small-data support, operand printing, scheduling and cost hooks, and other target hooks. The machine description files m32r.md, predicates.md, and constraints.md provide the RTL instruction patterns, operand predicates, constraint letters, and pipeline/scheduler attributes that drive instruction selection, recognition, shortening, and issue modeling for M32R variants. Target options and normalized option state are defined by m32r.opt and m32r-opts.h, while subtarget headers such as linux.h and little.h specialize the common backend for GNU/Linux integration and endian variants. Together, these file groups define how GCC lowers, optimizes, and emits code specifically for M32R processors, distinguishing this module from generic middle-end logic and from other target ports.
